status_summary: EPA announced a final rule on 2026-02-12 that rescinds the 2009 endangerment and cause-or-contribute findings and repeals all greenhouse gas emission standards for light-, medium- and heavy-duty vehicles and engines for model years 2012 and later; it was published 2026-02-18 and took effect 2026-04-20. This goes further than the Mandate's call to update the finding, and it leaves in place NHTSA's fuel economy program and, per a law firm summary, separate findings for stationary sources and aircraft engines. Challenges are pending in the D.C. Circuit (No. 26-1037 filed 2026-02-18 by health and environmental groups; No. 26-1061 filed 2026-03-19 by states and cities), and the latest docket summary found (through 2026-08-11) showed no ruling on a stay motion or on a 30-day abeyance motion filed 2026-07-29.

timeline.event: EPA publishes a notice of virtual public hearings (2025-08-19 and 2025-08-20) on its proposal to rescind the 2009 endangerment finding and repeal all vehicle greenhouse gas standards, citing Clean Air Act section 202(a) as the primary legal basis.

Final rule, Rescission of the Greenhouse Gas Endangerment Finding and Motor Vehicle Greenhouse Gas Emission Standards, is published (announced 2026-02-12 per a law firm alert); effective 2026-04-20. EPA's stated grounds are statutory interpretation, the major questions doctrine and a futility estimate; it did not finalize the alternative bases it had proposed (a scientific reassessment and a technology-based argument).
Seventeen health and environmental organizations file the first petition for review in the D.C. Circuit (American Public Health Association v. EPA, No. 26-1037).
A coalition led by the attorneys general of New York, Massachusetts, California and Connecticut files a second petition (No. 26-1061), joined by other states, cities and counties.
EPA and private respondent-intervenors oppose a motion to stay the final rule; petitioners reply 2026-07-16. No ruling on the stay motion appears in the docket summary found.
Most petitioners move for a 30-day abeyance so EPA can act on pending administrative reconsideration petitions (one filed 2026-04-16); EPA and intervenor states oppose on 2026-08-10.
